source: Requirements from FAR 52.204-21(b)(1), as adopted for CMMC Level 1 in 32 CFR Part 170. Practice identifiers follow the CMMC Level 1 Assessment Guide. Questions are plain-language aids written for this tool, not official assessment objectives.

practices.title: Authorized Access Control
practices.requirement: Limit information system access to authorized users, processes acting on behalf of authorized users, or devices (including other information systems).

questions.text: Do you keep a current list of the people and service accounts allowed to use the systems that store or process Federal Contract Information (FCI)?
questions.evidence: User list exported from your directory or a maintained spreadsheet.

questions.text: Do you keep a list of the devices (computers, phones, servers) allowed to connect to those systems?
questions.evidence: Device or asset inventory.

questions.text: Does every system require a sign-in, so only those listed users and devices can get in?
questions.evidence: Screenshots of sign-in settings; confirmation that guest or anonymous access is off.

practices.remediation: Create and maintain a list of authorized users and devices, turn off guest and anonymous access, and require a sign-in on every system that holds FCI.

practices.title: Transaction and Function Control
practices.requirement: Limit information system access to the types of transactions and functions that authorized users are permitted to execute.

questions.text: Have you defined what each type of user is allowed to do (for example, only administrators can install software or change settings)?
questions.evidence: Written roles or permission groups.

questions.text: Are everyday users prevented from having administrator rights on their computers?
questions.evidence: Local administrator group membership showing only IT staff.

practices.remediation: Define user roles, remove administrator rights from everyday accounts, and give administrators a separate account for admin work.

practices.title: External Connections
practices.requirement: Verify and control/limit connections to and use of external information systems.

questions.text: Have you identified the outside systems people use for company work, such as personal devices, home computers, cloud services, and customer or partner portals?
questions.evidence: List of approved external systems and services.

questions.text: Do you control or limit those connections, for example by allowing company data only on approved devices and services?
questions.evidence: Policy on personal devices and cloud services; device management or conditional access settings.

practices.remediation: List the external systems and services in use, approve the ones that are needed, and block or restrict company data on everything else.

practices.title: Control Public Information
practices.requirement: Control information posted or processed on publicly accessible information systems.

questions.text: Is there a named person who must approve what is posted on your website and social media?
questions.evidence: Named approvers and a short posting procedure.

questions.text: Is public content reviewed to make sure it contains no FCI, both before posting and periodically afterward?
questions.evidence: Review checklist or records of reviews.

practices.remediation: Name who may post public content, require review for FCI before anything is published, and check existing public content periodically.

practices.title: Identification
practices.requirement: Identify information system users, processes acting on behalf of users, or devices.

questions.text: Does every person have their own user account, with no shared logins?
questions.evidence: User account list showing one account per person.

questions.text: Are devices and service accounts uniquely named and recorded in your inventory or directory?
questions.evidence: Device inventory and list of service accounts.

practices.remediation: Replace shared logins with individual accounts and record every device and service account with a unique name.

practices.title: Authentication
practices.requirement: Authenticate (or verify) the identities of those users, processes, or devices, as a prerequisite to allowing access to organizational information systems.

questions.text: Must every user prove who they are, with a password or something stronger, before getting access?
questions.evidence: Sign-in and password policy settings.

questions.text: Are default passwords on new devices, software, and equipment changed before they are used?
questions.evidence: Setup checklist that includes changing default passwords.

practices.remediation: Require authentication on every system and change all default passwords; adding multi-factor authentication is strongly recommended and is required at Level 2.

practices.title: Media Disposal
practices.requirement: Sanitize or destroy information system media containing Federal Contract Information before disposal or release for reuse.

questions.text: Before throwing away hard drives, USB drives, phones, or paper containing FCI, do you securely wipe or destroy them?
questions.evidence: Disposal procedure and destruction certificates or log.

questions.text: Before a computer or drive is given to someone else or reused, is it securely wiped?
questions.evidence: Wipe procedure and records.

practices.remediation: Adopt a simple disposal procedure: wipe with an approved tool or physically destroy media, use a certified shredding vendor for paper, and keep a log.

practices.title: Limit Physical Access
practices.requirement: Limit physical access to organizational information systems, equipment, and the respective operating environments to authorized individuals.

questions.text: Have you decided who is allowed into the areas where your computers, servers, and network equipment are kept?
questions.evidence: List of people with access to offices and equipment rooms.

questions.text: Are those areas physically protected, for example with locked doors, badge access, or a locked server closet?
questions.evidence: Photos or description of locks and access controls.

practices.remediation: Define who may enter office and equipment areas, and lock the server or network closet and any area where FCI is handled.

practices.title: Manage Visitors and Physical Access
practices.requirement: Escort visitors and monitor visitor activity; maintain audit logs of physical access; and control and manage physical access devices.

questions.text: Are visitors escorted and supervised while they are in areas with company systems or FCI?
questions.evidence: Visitor procedure.

questions.text: Do you keep a visitor log or another record of who entered the facility and when?
questions.evidence: Visitor sign-in log or badge system records.

questions.text: Do you control keys, badges, and lock combinations: knowing who has them, collecting them when people leave, and changing combinations when needed?
questions.evidence: Key and badge issuance list.

practices.remediation: Escort visitors, keep a sign-in log, and track who holds keys and badges, collecting them at departure.

practices.title: Boundary Protection
practices.requirement: Monitor, control, and protect organizational communications (i.e., information transmitted or received by organizational information systems) at the external boundaries and key internal boundaries of the information systems.

questions.text: Is there a firewall between your internal network and the internet?
questions.evidence: Network diagram showing the firewall.

questions.text: Is the firewall set to block unnecessary incoming traffic, and are its settings and logs reviewed?
questions.evidence: Firewall rule export and review records.

practices.remediation: Put a business-grade firewall at the internet edge, block all inbound traffic that is not needed, and review its rules and alerts regularly.

practices.title: Public-Access System Separation
practices.requirement: Implement subnetworks for publicly accessible system components that are physically or logically separated from internal networks.

questions.text: If you run anything the public can reach (such as a website, file sharing server, or guest Wi-Fi), is it kept separate from your internal network, for example on its own network segment, a separate guest network, or hosted by a provider? Answer N/A only if you run nothing public-facing.
questions.evidence: Network diagram showing the separate segment or hosted service.

practices.remediation: Move public-facing services to a separate network segment or an external host, and put guest Wi-Fi on its own isolated network.

practices.title: Flaw Remediation
practices.requirement: Identify, report, and correct information and information system flaws in a timely manner.

questions.text: Do you have a way to learn about security flaws in the products you use, such as automatic update notices or vendor alerts?
questions.evidence: Update settings and subscribed vendor alerts.

questions.text: Do you install security updates for operating systems and software within a set time frame?
questions.evidence: Patch schedule and update history.

practices.remediation: Turn on automatic updates where possible, subscribe to vendor security alerts, and set a time frame for installing critical updates.

practices.title: Malicious Code Protection
practices.requirement: Provide protection from malicious code at appropriate locations within organizational information systems.

questions.text: Is antivirus or endpoint protection installed on every computer and server?
questions.evidence: Endpoint protection console showing all devices.

questions.text: Is incoming email filtered for malware and phishing?
questions.evidence: Email security settings.

practices.remediation: Deploy endpoint protection on every computer and server, and turn on malware and phishing filtering for email.

practices.title: Update Malicious Code Protection
practices.requirement: Update malicious code protection mechanisms when new releases are available.

questions.text: Does your antivirus or endpoint protection update itself automatically when new versions and definitions are released?
questions.evidence: Update settings and last-update dates in the console.

practices.remediation: Turn on automatic updates for endpoint protection and check the console for devices that are out of date.

practices.title: System and File Scanning
practices.requirement: Perform periodic scans of the information system and real-time scans of files from external sources as files are downloaded, opened, or executed.

questions.text: Does your antivirus run scheduled full scans of computers and servers?
questions.evidence: Scan schedule settings.

questions.text: Does it scan files in real time as they are downloaded, opened, or run, including files from USB drives and email?
questions.evidence: Real-time protection settings.

practices.remediation: Schedule regular full scans and make sure real-time protection is on for downloads, removable media, and email attachments.
